summary.intent: Run the GSD plan-phase and execute-phase workflows for Phase 45 of cipher-box — a Rust-only hygiene refactor of the FUSE write-journal/replay code — covering research, planning, verification, and wave-based execution.
summary.outcome: Planning completed fully (6 plans across 5 waves, verified, committed). Execution completed Waves 1–4 (plans 45-01 through 45-05); Wave 5 / plan 45-06 (consolidate fuser/winfsp journal builders into journal_helpers.rs) was in progress at the end of the transcript.

repo: The FUSE crate is `cipherbox-fuse` (default feature `fuse`), located at `crates/fuse/`.
`crates/fuse/src/fuse_abi.rs` carries pre-existing dead-code warnings from the vendored `fuser` ABI — unrelated to any phase work.
`crates/fuse/windows/mod.rs` is `cfg`-excluded on macOS, causing rust-analyzer 'unlinked-file' diagnostics that are expected and not errors.

The desktop consumer (`apps/desktop/src-tauri`) imports `JournalOp` from the SDK; changes to that field's type (e.g. `String` → `Option<String>` in 45-03) require a workspace-level check, not just the `cipherbox-fuse` crate check.
Plan 45-02 discovered a third duplicate of the journal-dir helper in `crates/fuse/src/fuse/windows/mod.rs` beyond the two called out in the plan — scope was widened correctly by the executor.

The GSD commit helper has a known false-negative: it returns `commit_failed` even when the commit succeeded (lint-staged output is misread as an error). Verify with `git log` rather than trusting the helper's return value.
The Rust API surface extractor returns 0 symbols for Rust crates — it only covers JS/TS; skip passing its output to the planner for Rust-only phases.
Waves 2–5 all serialized through `crates/fuse/src/lib.rs`; only Wave 1 (45-01 + 45-02) had zero file overlap, making worktree-based parallelism beneficial for just one wave.

code.finding: Post-45-03 IDE showed E0308 `expected Option<String> found String` here, but this was stale rust-analyzer cache from the executor's mid-edit state — `cargo check --workspace` confirmed clean.
Last file modified by plan 45-06 (consolidate fuser/winfsp journal builders into journal_helpers.rs) — execution status unknown at transcript end.

workflow: After executor subagents complete, always run `cargo check --workspace` (not just the target crate) to catch downstream type breakage; executors may only self-verify their own crate.
IDE diagnostics (rust-analyzer) can show false compile errors mid-execution because the analyzer caches mid-edit states; treat them as unconfirmed until `cargo check` corroborates.

For phases where only one wave has parallel plans and the rest are a serial chain on a single hot file (lib.rs), sequential execution on the feature branch is lower risk than worktrees despite `USE_WORKTREES=true`.
The GSD `--auto` flag suppresses the auto-advance confirmation prompt and chains planning directly into execution — useful for trusted phases but removes the human gate before Rust rewrites.
Post-merge gate pattern: spot-check executor SUMMARY + branch + commit count before proceeding to the next plan, especially when IDE diagnostics look alarming.

friction: GSD commit helper returned `commit_failed` false-negative on VALIDATION.md commit — required manual `git log` verification to confirm the commit landed (340e93efe).

After plan 45-03, rust-analyzer showed three compile errors (`read_ops.rs:821`, `macros.rs`, `mod.rs:59`) that appeared to be real failures; required running `cargo check --workspace` and `cargo test` to confirm they were stale IDE cache.

Executor for plan 45-03 only ran `cargo check` on `cipherbox-fuse` and `cipherbox-sdk`, not the full workspace — orchestrator had to run the workspace check itself to catch potential downstream breakage.

Rust API surface extractor silently returns empty (0 symbols) for Rust crates with no error, requiring the orchestrator to detect and skip it rather than surfacing a clear unsupported-language message.
